query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A tailored thermo-mechanical treatment consisting of cryo-rolling followed by controlled annealing will refine the lamellar microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA, thereby enhancing long-term resistance to room-temperature creep and corrosion while preserving strength and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
generation.intervention: Application of cryo-rolling (e.g., achieving an approximate 50% thickness reduction at liquid nitrogen temperature) followed by annealing at around 550°C for 30 minutes in an inert atmosphere.
generation.conditions: Processing under controlled temperature conditions to ensure uniform deformation and to avoid over-deformation or excessive recrystallization during annealing.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a hierarchically refined lamellar microstructure with ultrafine grains and stabilized phase boundaries that limit diffusion pathways.
generation.mechanism: Cryo-rolling induces high dislocation density and grain refinement without significant recovery, while subsequent annealing allows selective recrystallization and interface stabilization. The resultant refined microstructure impedes dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding, thereby reducing room-temperature creep and corrosion susceptibility.
generation.predicted_outcome: An enhancement in yield strength and ductility by an estimated 10–20% and improved resistance to room-temperature creep and corrosion compared to untreated samples.
generation.baseline: The original as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA lacking additional thermo-mechanical processing.
generation.boundary: This treatment’s benefits depend critically on the precise selection of deformation reduction and annealing parameters; over-annealing or excessive deformation may lead to grain coarsening or microstructural instability.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal combination of cryo-rolling reduction and annealing temperature/time to maximize long-term resistance to creep and corrosion without degrading ductility remains to be fully quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Process multiple sets of samples using varied cryo-rolling reductions (e.g., 30%, 50%, 70%) and different annealing temperatures/times. Characterize the microstructure (using EBSD and TEM), then perform room-temperature creep tests, corrosion tests in simulated environments, and tensile tests.
measurements: Grain size and phase boundary analysis via EBSD/TEM
Creep rate under constant load at room or moderately elevated temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermo-mechanically processed samples do not display statistically significant improvements in microstructural stability, creep resistance, or corrosion performance compared to untreated samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Nano-lamellar (L12 + B2) AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA) was processed by cryo-rolling and annealing. The EHEA developed a novel hierarchical microstructure featured by fine lamellar regions consisting of FCC lamellae filled with ultrafine FCC grains (average size ~200–250 nm) and B2 lamellae, and coarse non-lamellar regions consisting of ultrafine FCC (average size ~200–250 nm), few coarse recrystallized FCC grains and rather coarse unrecrystallized B2 phase (~2.5 µm). This complex and hierarchical microstructure originated from differences in strain-partitioning amongst the constituent phases, affecting the driving force for recrystallization. The hierarchical microstructure of the cryo-rolled and annealed material resulted in simultaneous enhancement in strength (Yield Strength/YS: 1437 ± 26 MPa, Ultimate Tensile Strength/UTS: 1562 ± 33 MPa) and ductility (elongation to failure/ef ~ 14 ± 1%) as compared to the as-cast as well as cold-rolled and annealed materials. The present study for the first time demonstrated that cryo-deformation and annealing could be a novel microstructural design strategy for overcoming strength-ductility trade off in multiphase high ent

Given the energy-efficient improvement and large safety factors, the attainment of high strength and high ductility in materials is arguably a vital requirement for most engineering applications. Unfortunately, these two properties are generally mutually exclusive, particularly in pure metals and alloys. Eutectic alloys specifically exhibit good liquidity and castability, preventing common casting flaws, like internal shrinkage and compositional segregation, to downgrade mechanical properties. They also possess a regularly arranged lamellar organization that can be viewed as a natural or in situ composite, which enables synergetic reinforcement to improve mechanical properties and sometimes bring unusual electrical, magnetic, and optical behaviors. Eutectic materials have therefore been investigated in diverse application fields, but traditionally, only certain eutectic systems have been of major commercial importance. Recently, eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), first proposed by Lu et al. in 2014, were designed based on the above eutectic-alloy concept.
